subject: determine optimal grid sampling size from spatial model

messages.author: 0e6a9745e02f8e5a
messages.subject: determine optimal grid sampling size from spatial model
parts:
Hey all,

I want to determine the optimal size of a sampling grid in order to capture spatial variation in a variable within a reasonable degree of certainty. I have 2 years of data already of pretty extensive sampling (not on a grid, but at a relatively fine spatial scale). I used the SPDE approach to estimate the spatial field and range parameter. My thought was I could use this information to get predicted variance across some region under different sampling grids (filled with dummy data at the nodes?). I could determine some level of variance that I'm happy with and see at which grid size the variance exceeds this threshold. I've seen this done with soil variables and they computed the mean Kriging variance across a sampling region at varying grid regions. Does this make sense? Does anyone have any suggestions about I would go about implementing this?

Thank you,
jordan

messages.author: 0e6a9745e02f8e5a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] determine optimal grid sampling size from spatial model
parts:
Sorry if I'm using terminology incorrectly--let me know where I can clarify better. To reiterate the objective, I want to be able to get some baseline estimate of a variable (insect abundance) across an entire region using the fewest number of sampling stations possible. The spatial intercept model that I ran estimates the range parameter to be pretty large, covering nearly the entire sampling area. My understanding of this is that predicted counts for a given area will be informed from sampling locations pretty far away, although I'm not sure how much information is shared exactly. I'm looking for a way to convince reviewers that a certain sampling grid (distance between sampling stations) will allow us to get estimates of a given variable in un-sampled areas within some degree of certainty? I am imagining a plot that shows uncertainty vs sampling grid density. Could I do this by making up data for different grids and re-running the model with a prior for the range parameter fixed at the estimates from the model using the real data? Then I'd take the mean 95% CI range (for example) from model.result$summary.linear.predictor across the entire mesh?

thanks,
jordan
